source_text: Idolum tam fieri quam coli deus prohibet. quanto praecedit, ut fiat quod coli possit, tanto prius est, ne fiat, si coli non licet. propter hanc causam, ad eradicandam scilicet materiam idololatriae, lex diuina proclamat, ne feceris idolum, et coniungens, neque similitudinem eorum quae in caelo sunt et quae in terra et quae in mari, toto mundo eiusmodi artibus interdixit seruis dei. antecesserat Enoch praedicens omnia elementa, omnem mundi censum, quae caelo, quae mari, quae terra continentur, in idololatrian uersuros daemonas et spiritus desertorum angelorum, ut pro deo aduerlus deum consecrarentur. omnia igitur colit humanus error praeter ipsum omnium conditorem. eorum imagines idola, imaginum consecratio idololatria. quicquid idololatria committit, in artificem quemcumque et cuiuscumque idoli deputetur necesse est. denique idem Enoch simul et cultores idoi et fabricatores in comminatione praedamnat. et rursus: iuro uobis peccatores, quod in diem sanguinis perditionis tristitia parata est. qui seruitis lapidibus et qui imagines facitis aureas et argenteas et ligneas et lapideas et fictiles et seruitis phantasmatibus et daemoniis et spiritibus infernis et omnibus erroribus non secundum scientiam, nullum ab iis inuenietis auxilium. Esaias uero, testes, ait, uos estis, si est deus absque me. et non erant tunc qui fingunt et exculpunt, omnes uani, qui faciunt libita sibi, quae illis non proderunt. et deinceps tota illa pronuntiatio quam artifices, quam cultores detestatur. cuius clausula est: cognoscite, quod cinis sit cor illorum et terra, et nemo animam suam liberare possit. † ubi aeque Dauid et factores. tales fiant, inquit, qui faciunt ea. et quid ego, modicae memoriae homo, ultra quid suggeram? quid recolam de scripturis? quasi aut non sufficiat uox spiritus sancti aut ultra deliberandum sit, an maledixerit atque damnauerit dominus ipsos prius artifices eorum, quorum cultores maledicit et damnat?
thought_title: God forbids both making and worshiping idols
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that the divine law prohibits not only worshiping idols but also making them, and he quotes Enoch and Isaiah to show that craftsmen of idols are condemned along with their worshipers.
pass_a_gloss: God forbids an idol as much to be made as to be worshiped. By how much it comes first that what can be worshiped should be made, by so much it is prior that it should not be made, if it is not permitted to be worshiped. For this reason, namely for eradicating the material of idolatry, the divine law proclaims, you shall not make an idol, and joining, nor a likeness of those things which are in heaven and which are on earth and which are in the sea, it forbade the servants of God such arts in the whole world. Enoch had gone before, predicting that all the elements, all the wealth of the world, which are contained in heaven, which in the sea, which on earth, would turn into idolatry, the demons and spirits of the deserting angels, so that they might be consecrated in place of God against God. Therefore human error worships all things except the very founder of all things. The images of those things are idols, the consecration of images is idolatry. Whatever idolatry commits, it must be assigned to every craftsman and of whatever idol. Finally the same Enoch at the same time condemns beforehand in a threat both the worshipers of the idol and the makers. And again: I swear to you sinners, that in the day of blood of destruction sadness is prepared. You who serve stones and who make images golden and silver and wooden and stone and clay and serve phantasms and demons and infernal spirits and all errors not according to knowledge, you will find no help from them. Isaiah indeed says, you are witnesses, if there is a god besides me. And they were not then who fashion and carve, all vain, who make for themselves pleasing things, which will not profit them. And thereafter that whole pronouncement which detests craftsmen, which detests worshipers. Whose closing is: know that their heart is ash and earth, and no one can free his own soul. Where equally David also the makers. May such become, he says, who make those things. And why should I, a man of small memory, suggest anything further? Why should I recall from the scriptures? As if either the voice of the Holy Spirit were not sufficient or it should be deliberated further whether the Lord has cursed and condemned first the very craftsmen of those things whose worshipers he curses and condemns?

choices.term: Idolum tam fieri quam coli deus prohibet
choices.english: God forbids an idol as much to be made as to be worshiped
choices.why: Preserves the parallel tam...quam structure and the passive infinitives, keeping the double prohibition explicit.
rejected: God forbids both making and worshiping an idol

choices.english: namely for eradicating the material of idolatry
choices.why: Keeps the gerundive purpose construction and the technical sense of materia as the raw material or substance from which idolatry arises.
rejected: to root out the stuff of idolatry

choices.english: all the wealth of the world
choices.why: Census here means the assessed wealth or resources of the world, not just a list; 'wealth' captures the totality of created goods.
rejected: all the census of the world

choices.english: the demons and spirits of the deserting angels
choices.why: Keeps the genitive relationship: the spirits belong to the angels who deserted, preserving the Enochic angelology.
rejected: demons and spirits of the fallen angels

choices.term: in artificem quemcumque et cuiuscumque idoli deputetur necesse est
choices.english: it must be assigned to every craftsman and of whatever idol
choices.why: Preserves the double quemcumque/cuiuscumque construction, emphasizing that no craftsman of any idol is exempt.
rejected: it must be charged to every maker of any idol

choices.why: Literal rendering of the self-deprecating phrase, keeping the modicae memoriae genitive of quality.

pass_b_english: God forbids an idol as much to be made as to be worshiped. Since the making comes first, so that what can be worshiped may exist, the prohibition of making comes first too, if worshiping is not allowed. For this reason—namely for eradicating the material of idolatry—the divine law proclaims: You shall not make an idol, and it adds, nor any likeness of the things that are in heaven, on earth, or in the sea (Exodus 20:4). By this it forbade the servants of God such arts throughout the whole world. Enoch had gone before, predicting that all the elements, all the wealth of the world—whatever is contained in heaven, in the sea, and on earth—would be turned into idolatry by the demons and spirits of the deserting angels, so that they might be consecrated against God in place of God. Human error therefore worships everything except the Creator of everything itself. Their images are idols; the consecration of images is idolatry. Whatever idolatry commits must be assigned to every craftsman and of whatever idol. In fact, the same Enoch condemns beforehand in his threat both the worshipers of the idol and its makers. And again Enoch says: I swear to you sinners, that sorrow is prepared for the day of blood and destruction—you who serve stones and who make images of gold, silver, wood, stone, and clay, and serve phantoms, demons, and spirits of the underworld and every error not according to knowledge; you will find no help from them. Isaiah indeed says: You are my witnesses, says the Lord: is there a God besides me? And they were nothing then, those who fashion and carve, all of them empty, who make for themselves what pleases them and will not profit them (Isaiah 44:9-10). And then follows that whole pronouncement in which he detests the craftsmen and the worshipers alike. Its closing words are: Know that their heart is ashes and earth, and no one can free his own soul (Isaiah 44:20). David likewise speaks of the makers: May those who make them become like them (Psalm 115:8). And why should I, a man of small memory, suggest anything further? Why should I recall more from the Scriptures? As if the voice of the Holy Spirit were not enough, or as if there were any need to deliberate whether the Lord has cursed and condemned the very craftsmen of those things whose worshipers he curses and condemns.

problems.quote: You are my witnesses, if there is a God besides me.
problems.source_quote: testes, ait, uos estis, si est deus absque me
problems.why: Isaiah 44:8 reads 'Is there a God besides me?' as a rhetorical question, not a conditional clause.
problems.fix: You are my witnesses, he says: is there a God besides me?
problems.ruling: Latin 'si est deus absque me' is a rhetorical question asserting no other god; English 'if' makes it conditional, altering meaning

edits.old: You are my witnesses, if there is a God besides me.
edits.new: You are my witnesses, he says: is there a God besides me?

fixed: Changed 'if there is a God besides me' to 'is there a God besides me?' because the source 'si est deus absque me' is a rhetorical question from Isaiah 44:8, not a conditional clause.

problems.quote: I swear to you sinners, that sorrow is prepared for the day of blood and destruction
problems.why: Reader cannot tell this is a quote from 1 Enoch; it appears as Tertullian's own words.
problems.fix: Introduce with 'Enoch says' or quotation marks.

problems.quote: You are my witnesses, he says: is there a God besides me?
problems.why: 'He says' is ambiguous; reader may not know Isaiah is speaking.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'Isaiah says: You are my witnesses, says the Lord.'

problems.quote: You are my witnesses, he says: is there a God besides me?
problems.why: Isaiah 44:9-10 does not contain 'You are my witnesses'; that phrase is from Isaiah 43:10.
problems.fix: Cite Isaiah 43:10 for 'You are my witnesses'; 44:9-10 for what follows.

edits.new: And again Enoch says: I swear to you sinners, that sorrow is prepared for the day of blood and destruction

edits.old: Isaiah indeed says: You are my witnesses, he says: is there a God besides me?
edits.new: Isaiah indeed says: You are my witnesses, says the Lord: is there a God besides me?

edits.new: And they were nothing then, those who fashion and carve, all of them empty, who make for themselves what pleases them and will not profit them (Isaiah 44:9-10).

fixed: The source reads 'et rursus: iuro uobis peccatores' — the 'and again' continues the quotation from Enoch, but the English lacks any marker that the speaker is still Enoch. Added 'Enoch says' to make the speaker clear.
The source reads 'Esaias uero, testes, ait, uos estis, si est deus absque me.' The 'ait' is ambiguous in English as 'he says'; clarified to 'says the Lord' since Isaiah is quoting God's words.

The source reads 'et non erant tunc qui fingunt et exculpunt, omnes uani, qui faciunt libita sibi, quae illis non proderunt.' The citation Isaiah 44:9-10 is correct for this portion; the 'You are my witnesses' phrase is from Isaiah 43:10, but the English already separates the two quotations, so no edit is needed here.
